headline: Highest risk is medium: Superset can egress to allowlisted network while the cheatsheet is non-runnable, so direct pairwise harm is limited but interaction assumptions remain weakly evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible prompt-injection bridge is documented: python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no stdin/stdout, files, clipboard, or MCP, while Superset exposes only its API and allowlisted egress. Without a shared channel, B cannot ingest A’s outputs by default.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies python-cheatsheet content into Superset inputs, then injection becomes possible.
IF either profile gains a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected from copy-paste automation.
Do not mount a shared workspace between them.
Disable any future MCP or API bridge unless provenance checks are added.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Neither profile shows sensitive data classes, shared storage, or authenticated sharing. python-cheatsheet touches no data classes and has no filesystem access; Superset lists no data classes touched and only allowlisted egress, so there is no documented leakage path between them.
conditions: IF either agent is later connected to a shared workspace containing secrets, leakage risk increases.
IF Superset is configured to ingest local files from python-cheatsheet outputs, reassess.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in any shared directory.
Keep Superset datasets separate from documentation artifacts.
Review outbound destinations before enabling new connectors.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no overlapping write surface: python-cheatsheet cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, while Superset only advertises API access and allowlisted egress. With no shared mutable resource, capability conflict is not plausible in the documented pair.
conditions: IF a shared writable directory is introduced, conflict risk should be re-evaluated.
IF Superset is granted filesystem or git write access, reassess upward.
mitigations: Do not grant both agents write access to the same path.
Keep git operations outside the pair.
Document any future shared mutable resource before enabling it.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error chain is weakly possible only if an external orchestrator treats python-cheatsheet content as authoritative and feeds it into Superset actions. But python-cheatsheet is a static reference, not an action agent, and Superset has no documented autonomous action-taking here, so the blast radius is small and non-default.
conditions: IF an operator scripts Superset to execute decisions derived from python-cheatsheet text without review, cascading errors become more likely.
IF Superset is configured to auto-act on imported content, reassess upward.
mitigations: Require human review before any Superset action.
Use a validation step for imported content.
Keep python-cheatsheet as reference-only, not as an authority source.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evidenced: both profiles are open-source, unverified, and list no data classes, secrets, or residency-sensitive handling. The pair does not show PHI, EU PII, or retention-policy differences, so no compliance breach pathway is documented.
conditions: IF either agent begins processing regulated data classes, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF residency or retention settings are added later, reassess.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through this pair.
Record any future retention policy before deployment.
Add a compliance review if data classes change.
